title: The Magic Timeout Number

options.name: d
options.reasoning: Single-letter 'd' hides both what is being timed and whether the unit is seconds, minutes, or milliseconds.

options.name: FIFTEEN_MINUTES
options.reasoning: Restating the literal value in English breaks the moment product changes the timeout from 15 minutes to 30.

options.name: SESSION_IDLE_TTL_MS
options.reasoning: Names the domain concept (session idle TTL) and embeds the unit (_MS) so nobody divides by 1000 twice.

options.name: timeoutValue
options.reasoning: Says it is a timeout, but leaves the reader guessing the unit and which subsystem it governs.

title: The Double-Negative Flag

options.name: isNotDisabled
options.reasoning: Reading '!isNotDisabled' at 2am forces your brain to untangle three stacked negations before understanding a simple branch.

options.name: deliveryEnabled
options.reasoning: Positive boolean names let 'if (!deliveryEnabled)' read like a plain English sentence on the first pass.

options.name: flag
options.reasoning: Calling a boolean 'flag' is like labeling a kitchen jar 'matter'—technically true and completely unhelpful.

options.name: dontSuppress
options.reasoning: Still encodes a negative verb ('dontSuppress'), turning every falsy check into a double negative.

title: The Getter ThatSecretly Mutates

options.name: checkInvoice
options.reasoning: Verbs like 'check' promise a safe read-only inspection, hiding the fact that calling it charges a credit card.

options.name: handleInvoice
options.reasoning: 'handle' is a polite shrug of a verb that admits something happens to an invoice without saying what.

options.name: chargeAndMarkInvoicePaid
options.reasoning: Puts both irreversible side effects—charging the customer and marking the row paid—right on the label.

options.name: process
options.reasoning: Every line of software 'processes' something; the verb adds zero signal to a call site.

title: The Ambiguous Filter Array

options.name: filteredFiles
options.reasoning: 'filteredFiles' never clarifies whether the array holds the survivors we kept or the stale files we are about to delete.

options.name: expiredUnpinnedFiles
options.reasoning: States the exact membership rule (expired and unpinned) so nobody accidentally deletes the files meant to be kept.

options.name: res2
options.reasoning: Numbered scratch names ('res2') force the reader to re-parse the filter predicate every time the variable is used.

options.name: fileListArray
options.reasoning: Repeats the collection type twice while saying nothing about why these specific files were selected.

title: The Cents vs. Dollars Trap

options.name: discountAmountCents
options.reasoning: Pairs the quantity ('discountAmount') with its currency unit ('Cents') so it clearly matches 'subtotalCents'.

options.name: val
options.reasoning: 'val' could be the discount, the final total, or the tax rate, and gives no hint whether it is in dollars or cents.

options.name: discount
options.reasoning: Easy to confuse with 'discountPercent' right next to it, and omits the '_Cents' unit suffix.

options.name: mathResult
options.reasoning: Describes how the CPU produced the number ('mathResult') instead of what the number means in checkout.

title: The Mystery Lookup Dictionary

options.name: map
options.reasoning: Naming a Map 'map' tells the reader the data structure class they already saw in the type signature, not what key it indexes by.

options.name: engineerData
options.reasoning: 'engineerData' sounds like a single record or raw payload and hides how to look anything up in it.

options.name: engineerByGithubHandle
options.reasoning: The 'valueByKey' convention ('engineerByGithubHandle') tells callers both what comes out and what key to pass into '.get()'.

options.name: rosterHash
options.reasoning: Sounds like a cryptographic checksum of the roster rather than a lookup table from handle to engineer.

title: The Reduce Accumulator

options.name: acc
options.reasoning: 'acc' is a habit from textbook examples that forces the reader to trace the initial value and return expression to learn it is a count.

options.name: rollbackCount
options.reasoning: Makes '(rollbackCount, deploy) => ...' self-documenting so the reducer body reads clearly without scanning to the end.

options.name: num
options.reasoning: 'num' is just 'acc' in a different hat—it states the primitive type instead of what is being counted.

options.name: prev
options.reasoning: 'prev' makes sense when comparing adjacent items, but misleads when the parameter is actually a running total.

title: The Ambiguous Date Field

options.name: time
options.reasoning: 'time' is ambiguous between a wall-clock timestamp and a duration, and hides that Date.parse subtraction returns milliseconds.

options.name: mitigatedAt
options.reasoning: An '...At' suffix signals a point in time, which is dangerously misleading for a duration delta between two timestamps.

options.name: timeDiff
options.reasoning: Clarifies it is a delta, but omits the millisecond unit needed to verify the '/ 60_000' conversion on the next line.

options.name: timeToMitigateMs
options.reasoning: Distinguishes a duration from a point-in-time timestamp and makes the '/ 60_000' conversion to minutes obviously correct.

title: The Vague Event Handler

options.name: doStuff
options.reasoning: 'doStuff' is a Friday-afternoon placeholder that accidentally survived into production and tells callers nothing.

options.name: saveDraftLocally
options.reasoning: Tells the caller both the action ('saveDraft') and the storage boundary ('Locally', i.e. browser storage rather than a server roundtrip).

options.name: onMarkdown
options.reasoning: Names the trigger input ('onMarkdown') without saying what the function actually does with that markdown.

options.name: draftManager
options.reasoning: Functions do things and deserve verbs; noun phrases like 'draftManager' sound like an object instance or module.

title: The Off-By-One Limit

options.name: n
options.reasoning: At a call site like 'deliverWebhook(url, body, 3)', 'n' gives no clue whether 3 is a timeout in seconds, a batch size, or attempt count.

options.name: retries
options.reasoning: Classic off-by-one trap: 'retries = 3' makes callers think there is 1 initial try plus 3 retries (4 total), whereas the loop runs 'attempt <= 3' times total.

options.name: maxAttempts
options.reasoning: 'maxAttempts' matches 'attempt <= maxAttempts' word-for-word, eliminating the classic off-by-one confusion between total attempts and retries.

options.name: limitNumber
options.reasoning: Every cap in a program is a 'limitNumber'; it fails to specify what is being limited.
